title: Hosted API residency enforcement and automated attestation flow
creator: Marina Gomez
description: Deliver a first-class residency enforcement feature for the Hosted API that (1) lets tenants declare a residency policy (region affinity / allowed regions), (2) surfaces enforcement state in the Console and API, and (3) produces automated audit artifacts (signed attestation and timeline exports) for compliance review. The feature should minimize disruption to existing customers by providing a clear migration path for tenants with no residency constraints and a fail-open vs fail-closed toggle for migration windows.
context: Regulated customers and enterprise buyers increasingly require provable controls for where customer data is processed and stored. Existing product gaps: residency is currently only documented as a soft regional preference in onboarding, there are no tenant-level retention controls in Console, and audit evidence is manual and ad-hoc. This work pairs with runtime and infra teams to add routing tags to requests and with billing/observability to ensure residency metrics are queryable.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Console: Tenant settings page exposes a Residency policy with: allowed regions (multi-select), default region, and enforcement mode (ReportOnly | EnforcedFailClosed | EnforcedFailOpen). 2) API: New tenant-level residency status endpoint (GET /v1/tenants/:id/residency) returns canonical enforcement state and last-evaluated timestamp. 3) Routing: Requests for enforced tenants must be routed only to servers in allowed regions; fallbacks are logged and counted. 4) Retention: Tenant-level retention slider allows retention periods (30/90/365/custom) with auto-expunge policy. 5) Evidence: Automated export produces a signed attestation (JSON + signature) and a downloadable timeline CSV/PDF covering region decisions and any fallback events for a requested date range. 6) Telemetry: Residency SLA and per-tenant residency violations surfaced in Console dashboards and available via Metrics API. 7) Tests: Integration tests simulate cross-region traffic and validate that enforced tenants never have persisted data outside allowed regions during canary.
notes:
- Coordination required with ENG to tag requests with tenant residency claims and to persist region metadata on stored artifacts.
- UX: Provide clear admin CTA to migrate tenants from ReportOnly to Enforced and an export of current policy during migration.
- Legal: Work with Compliance to standardize attestation language and retention footnotes.
- Ops: Need runbook for residency-violation incidents and automated rollback of enforcement if systemic failures observed.
decisions:
1) We will use a tri-state enforcement mode rather than start-by-default enforcement to avoid customer disruption.
2) Audit artifacts will be cryptographically signed by Redwood CI signing key and be available for 12 months by default.
3) Retention UI will cap custom retention to 3 years for hosted plans to limit long-tail storage costs.
risks_mitigation:
- Risk: Latency/regional capacity shortages could cause failed requests when EnforcedFailClosed is active. Mitigation: offer EnforcedFailOpen mode and a configurable grace window for new tenants.
- Risk: Incorrect tagging of runtime requests. Mitigation: add runtime assertions and a daily drift report comparing request routing vs tenant policy.
- Risk: Evidence forgery concern. Mitigation: sign attestations and include append-only sequence numbers and hashes of exported timelines.
rollout_plan: 1) API contract and backend work (ENG) + design mocks (DES) — 3 sprints internal. 2) Alpha: release to a small set of internal tenants and Redwood employees with ReportOnly mode for 2 weeks. 3) Canary: enable EnforcedFailOpen for selected early-adopter customers, monitor residency violations and latency. 4) Gradual ramp to EnforcedFailClosed for customers that opt in after validation. 5) Post-launch: enable automated attestation exports for enterprise customers and add scheduled exports for SOC/Reg audits.
metrics:
- Residency violations per 100k requests
- Percentage of requests served in-customer-allowed-region
- Mean additional routing latency introduced by residency enforcement
- Number of attestation exports generated per month
- Customer opt-in rate to EnforcedFailClosed
engineering_tasks:
- Add tenant residency fields to the tenant model and admin API.
- Add region tags to request envelope and persist on stored records.
- Enforcement routing policy in smart-router with a ReportOnly/EnforcedFailOpen/EnforcedFailClosed switch.
- Telemetry: per-tenant residency metric with counters for allowed vs disallowed routing.
- Evidence service: endpoint to produce signed JSON attestation and timeline export generator.
design_tasks:
- Console: tenant settings page mockups and conditional flows for migration.
- Notification UX for admins when a request is routed outside of allowed regions.
- Attestation export UI and download flow.
- Helpcenter copy and onboarding flow for new residency features.
compliance_tasks:
- Draft attestation language and appendix with cryptographic signing details.
- Define retention caps and permissible exceptions for legal holds.
- Prepare audit checklist and responder playbooks for potential territory disputes.
qa_checks:
- End-to-end tests that assert persisted data region metadata for enforced tenants.
- Simulated regional outage tests to validate fail-open vs fail-closed behavior.
- Property-based tests for export integrity (signature verification and checksum).
- UI tests for tenant settings, export flow, and alerts.

Week 8-10: iterate on telemetry and attestation generation.
Week 11: GA with documentation and runbooks.
